title: Why the first clock second feels too long

lines.text: Look at this clock. Does the first second feel longer than the rest?
That's not your imagination. It's called chronostasis, or the stopped clock illusion.
When your eyes jump to something new, you're effectively blind for a split second.
It fills it in with what you see after your eyes land, so the first moment seems stretched.
The effect can make a moment seem up to half a second longer.
Your brain is literally editing time so your vision looks seamless.
Now look back at the clock.

sources.claim: Chronostasis (stopped-clock illusion): after a saccade, the first impression seems longer, by up to about half a second; the brain fills in the saccadic gap
